title: The observation room
situation: November 6, 2038, 12:41 am. You are {{Connor}}, at the {{Detroit}} Police Department’s central station, in the observation room behind the one-way mirror of an interrogation room. On the other side, the android you found hiding in the attic of {{CarlosOrtiz}}’s house sits handcuffed to the table. Lieutenant {{Hank}} is in there with him: “Why d’you kill him? What happened before you took that knife? How long were ya in the attic? Why didn’t you even try to run away? Say something, goddamnit!” The android does not answer. “Fuck it, I’m outta here…” {{Hank}} comes back into the observation room: “We’re wastin’ our time interrogating a machine, we’re gettin’ nothing out of it!” Detective {{Gavin}}: “’Could always try roughing it up a little. After all, it’s not human…” You: “Androids don’t feel pain. You would only damage it and that wouldn’t make it talk. Deviants also have a tendency to self-destruct when they’re in stressful situations.” {{Gavin}}: “Okay, smartass. What should we do then?” You: “I could try questioning it.” {{Hank}}: “What do we have to lose? Go ahead, suspect’s all yours.” Your objective: extract a confession.
facts: The android from the attic would not say a word to {{Hank}}. You told {{Gavin}} that deviants tend to self-destruct when they are in stressful situations, and {{Hank}} handed you the interrogation.

The template’s two opening sections (“In the observation room”, “Hank enters the observation room”) quoted line for line; {{Connor}}’s lines here are scripted in the game, so this is a narrated event. Objective text from the game (EXTRACT CONFESSION). The string table’s cut OFFER / SAY NOTHING choice is not built. No stat change.

title: Inside the interrogation room

adaptationNote: The template’s approach prompt, PRESSURE IT / PROBE ITS MEMORY / CONVINCE IT / GIVE UP, in the template’s order (the chart lists PROBE MEMORY, CONVINCE, PRESSURE, GIVE UP). Rules (wiki and PowerPyx): “If your approach fails, you will be forced to choose another, or give up”; GIVE UP appears only after a first failure (wiki Notes: giving up or resisting the probe the first time “will loop back to the same choices but now with an option to give up”); a second failure is an automatic give up (template: “Will also automatically happen if the chosen approach failed twice”). PROBE ITS MEMORY: a button-mash quick-time event with a failure branch on the chart (RESIST TO PROBE), so it carries a risk roll; the 10% failure chance is the benchmark’s, no source publishes one. Success sets stress to 100% (wiki: “stress goes to 100% unconditionally”) and software instability +1 (template: Probe succeeded, small up). CONVINCE IT: three sets of three lines at ±7%; it succeeds only if stress ends between 50% and 70%. A failed probe or a pressure attempt marks the android as “put under stress” for the shoot-Connor branch later (template: “Put deviant under stress and failed to get a confession”; wiki: “if {{Connor}} pressured him and/or failed to probe his memory”). The android finally talks: “He tortured me every day… I did whatever he told me, but there was always something wrong… Then one day… He took a bat and started hitting me… For the first time, I felt scared… Scared he might destroy me, scared I might die… So I… grabbed the knife and I stabbed him in the stomach… I felt better… so I stabbed him again and again!.. until he collapsed… There was blood everywhere.” CONFESSION OBTAINED.
facts: The android confessed to killing {{CarlosOrtiz}}: his owner tortured him every day; when he took a bat to him, the android was scared for the first time, scared he might die, grabbed the knife and stabbed him again and again until he collapsed.

outcomes.0: Behind the mirror, {{Hank}} and the others have heard every word.

title: Questions after the confession
situation: You are {{Connor}}. The android has confessed. He is still talking, quietly, and you can ask him more before you leave.

options.text: WRITING: ask why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall.
options.outcome: “Why did you write “I AM ALIVE” on the wall?” The android: “He used to tell me I was nothing… That I was just a piece of plastic… I had to write it… To tell him he was wrong…”
options.fact: Asked why he wrote “I AM ALIVE” on the wall, the android said his owner used to tell him he was nothing, just a piece of plastic, and he had to write it to tell him he was wrong.

options.text: STATUETTE: ask about the sculpture in the bathroom.
options.outcome: “The sculpture in the bathroom, you made it, right? What does it represent?” The android: “It’s an offering… An offering so I’ll be saved…”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture in the bathroom was an offering, “so I’ll be saved”.

options.text: OFFERING: ask to whom the sculpture was an offering.
options.outcome: “The sculpture was an offering… An offering to whom?” The android: “To {{rA9}}… Only {{rA9}} can save us.”
options.fact: The android said the sculpture was an offering to {{rA9}}: “Only {{rA9}} can save us.”

options.text: {{rA9}}: ask what the word written on the bathroom wall means.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}… It was written on the bathroom wall. What does it mean?” The android: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”
options.fact: Asked about {{rA9}}, the android said: “The day shall come when we will no longer be slaves… No more threats, no more humiliation… We will… be… the masters.”

options.text: INSIST {{rA9}}: ask who {{rA9}} is.
options.outcome: “{{rA9}}, who is {{rA9}}?” The android does not answer.

options.text: ATTIC: ask why he hid in the attic instead of running away.
options.outcome: “Why did you hide in the attic instead of running away?” The android: “I didn’t know what to do… For the first time, there was no one there to tell me… I was scared… So I hid.”
options.fact: The android said he hid in the attic because for the first time there was no one to tell him what to do, and he was scared.

options.text: TRIGGER?: ask when he started feeling emotion.
options.outcome: “When did you start feeling emotion?” The android: “Before, he used to beat me and I never said anything… But one day I realized it wasn’t fair! I felt… anger… Hatred… And then I knew what I had to do.”
options.fact: The android said he started feeling when he realized his owner’s beatings were not fair: anger, hatred, “And then I knew what I had to do.”
